clue.text: Regret having ordered variable, boring Rebus novel about hard-drinking copper

indicators.note: one thing boring into another sits inside it, so the variable goes into the rearranged letters
novel as an adjective means new or reworked, so the letters of Rebus are rearranged

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic variable
RE is Latin for about, concerning
Inspector Morse, Colin Dexter's fictional Oxford detective, was famously fond of beer

explanation.surface: A crime-fiction fan regrets buying an Ian Rankin Rebus book about a boozy detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' turns REBUS into BUERS, and 'boring' puts Y inside it to make BUYERS. Rebus is Ian Rankin's Edinburgh detective, a nice match for Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the regret a shopper feels after making a purchase they wish they had not.

clue.text: Heads of local football association hosted by an icon of Manchester City

indicators.note: something hosted by another is held within it, so the initials sit inside the footballer's name

parts.note: George Best, the Manchester United winger, is a footballing icon of that city

indicators.note: heads are the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Local football officials welcome a Manchester City legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manchester City' reads as one club, but the definition is just 'City'; the icon is George Best, who was born in this city and played for Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is the capital and largest urban centre of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Royal couple modelling hosiery going round county

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the pair of royal letters, enclosing them
modelling means shaping, so the letters of hosiery are reshaped

parts.note: a couple of royal abbreviations: R for rex and K for king

explanation.surface: A royal pair showing off stockings while touring an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'modelling' is the anagram signal and 'going round' the container. R (rex) and K (king) are a couple of royal abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire is the largest historic county in northern England.

clue.text: Wet fish to eat at home

indicators.note: a fish eating something takes it inside, so the home word goes into the fish

parts.note: a ray is a flat cartilaginous fish
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Damp fish to have for dinner at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainy weather is wet weather, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Record list

definitions.meaning: to record officially, as a birth or a vote
an official list, as of electors or pupils

explanation.surface: A bare pair of words meaning a written record or roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a register is a roll of names, and registering something records it.

clue.text: PM is hapless — trousers a disaster

indicators.note: as a verb, trousers means pockets, so the phrase keeps the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A luckless Prime Minister's choice of trousers proves a fashion disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a noun about clothing, but it is a verb meaning pockets: the answer sits inside 'PM is hapless'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident; calling it a disaster is a mild crossword stretch of the sense.

clue.text: Israel GNP revised, getting weaker again

indicators.note: economic figures that are revised get reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Israel's gross national product figures are revised downward, showing a weakening economy again.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient relapsing falls back into illness after improving, sliding back into a weaker condition.

clue.text: Her Majesty embracing the mythical concept of heaven

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the queen's initials wrap round the word

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen holds the myth of a heavenly realm.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient belief the ether was the pure upper air filling the heavens, where the gods lived.

clue.text: It cools grid forged in iron

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in the chemical symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, from Latin ferrum

indicators.note: forged means hammered into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cooling grate is made in a blacksmith's forge from iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges the grid letters and 'in' places them inside the symbol for iron; 'It' is the subject standing for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator is the household appliance that keeps food cool.

clue.text: Acting playfully, legendary US TV host forgets lines

indicators.note: a host who forgets something leaves it out, so these letters go missing

parts.note: Larry King hosted a long-running CNN talk show
RY, short for railway, means lines in crosswords

explanation.surface: A famous American chat-show host clowning around after fluffing his script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgets' takes RY out of LARRY KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Larking about is fooling around in high spirits, behaving playfully.

clue.text: An element of vitriol?

parts.note: oil of vitriol is an old name for a strong mineral acid, so the clue asks for one chemical element inside it, while vitriol also suggests venomous words

explanation.surface: Asks what part of someone's bitter abuse is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vitriol' reads as harsh words; chemically it is a strong acid made of hydrogen, oxygen and the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow non-metal is a chemical element present in the acid once called oil of vitriol.

clue.text: Test idiot. Always

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ay, also spelt aye, is an old and poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A schoolchild branded a fool in every exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is an analysis testing a metal or substance for purity.

clue.text: Ran off emotionally damaged, clutching empty purse

indicators.note: clutching means holding within, so the outer word wraps round the purse letters

parts.note: scarred describes someone left damaged by a bad experience

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters, the contents removed

explanation.surface: A traumatised mugger fled holding a purse with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps the ends of the purse and 'clutching' is the container. Scarper is British slang for run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for fleeing in a hurry, so scarpered means fled.

clue.text: Make fun of Charlie, that female bird- fancier

parts.note: to twit is to tease or taunt someone
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: Mocking a man named Charlie, and the woman who fancies birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' in British slang can be a woman, so 'bird-fancier' suggests a womaniser; a twitcher is a keen birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is a dedicated birdwatcher who travels to spot rare species.

clue.text: I am aching to travel somewhere in Asia

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A restless person longs to go on a trip to Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiang Mai is a city in northern Thailand, a popular destination in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Elevated seats for The Ring?

definitions.meaning: the raised tier of seats in a theatre above the stalls
the question mark flags the Wagner opera cycle as misdirection

explanation.surface: Choosing upstairs tickets for Wagner's Ring cycle at the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatre's raised balcony tier is the circle, and any ring is a circle in shape.

clue.text: Conservative corrupt politics down south involving male taking part in dodgy activity

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the male letter goes inside the rearranged letters
corrupt means twisted out of true, so these letters are rearranged
here down means knocked out, so the compass letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A Tory's crooked politics in the south of England draw a man into shady dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' drops S from POLITICS; 'corrupt' rearranges POLITIC, and 'involving' puts M inside, giving OMPLICIT after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone complicit is involved with others in wrongdoing, an accomplice to the crime.

clue.text: Art of Chinese engineer; quiet, upper- class entering Grand Prix

indicators.note: the three pieces enter the motor-racing letters, sitting inside them

parts.note: Grand Prix racing is Formula One, F1, with the 1 read as the letter I
SH is the call for quiet
U means upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: A Chinese engineer, a quiet posh type, joins a Formula One race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art of Chinese engineer' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Chinese'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feng shui is the Chinese practice of arranging surroundings to harmonise energy flow.

clue.text: Show faith in sacred Italian collects

indicators.note: the phrase collects the answer, holding it among its letters

explanation.surface: Believing in an Italian holy man who takes the church collection.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a claim is to believe it, putting trust in its truth.

clue.text: Caught hospital A&E in the US masking internet protocol code

indicators.note: masking means covering, so the outer letters hide the internet letters inside

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an American accident and emergency department is the ER, emergency room

explanation.surface: A hospital emergency team hides an internet address code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masking' is the container: the internet letters go after the C, not inside the American emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a secret code used to disguise a message.

clue.text: British Energy unit regularly farms out oil producer

parts.note: the erg is a unit of energy in the old CGS system

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A British energy company contracting out its farms to grow oil crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'farms out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot orange yields an aromatic essential oil used to flavour Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: The Speaker, possibly a user of a social medium?

definitions.meaning: a small loudspeaker for high frequencies

definitions.text: a user of a social medium?

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker might be posting on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Speaker' suggests the presiding officer of the House of Commons; it is a hi-fi loudspeaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is both a treble loudspeaker and a person who posts on Twitter.

clue.text: Angry denunciation of reported attack in 14?

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the answer sounds like the phrase

parts.note: 14 down is a Thai city, so an attack there would be a Thai raid

explanation.surface: A furious complaint about a news report of an assault in Chiang Mai.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 down is CHIANG MAI, in Thailand, so a raid there is a Thai raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long, angry speech of criticism or condemnation.

clue.text: Being dad, puffing when touring Rome on vacation

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the gasping word goes round the city letters

parts.note: panting and puffing both mean breathing hard

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the city keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Out of breath while showing the kids round Rome on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties Rome to its outer letters and 'touring' puts them inside the puffing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Parenting is raising children, the job of being a mother or father.

clue.text: Run over, step, run over

indicators.note: over at the end means turned over, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a pace is a single step
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Instructions like a training drill: run, step, run again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' at the end reverses PACE + R. The first 'run over' means go over again briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to go over the main points again, a summary review.

clue.text: Rubbish leader of government consumed by peevishness

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed inside it

parts.note: bile means bad temper or irritability

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Dismissing as nonsense a prime minister eaten up by bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is slang for nonsense, from the dirty water collecting in a ship's hull.

clue.text: Tossing — I note — 1lb pancake

indicators.note: tossing the letters throws them about, as one tosses a pancake

parts.note: the digit 1 is read as the letter I, and lb is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: A cook flipping a pound-weight pancake, noting it aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossing' rearranges ILB (1 read as I, plus lb for pound) into BLI; only the pound is tossed, the rest are set in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small Russian buckwheat pancakes, often served with caviar.

clue.text: Hence comic may get unlimited paeans?

indicators.note: without limits means each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: So a comedian may be showered with praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips the ends from each word: ENC, OMI and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomia, the plural of encomium, are speeches of high praise, like paeans.

clue.text: Perhaps no2 husband censored following broadcast

indicators.note: following places the censored word after the broadcast one

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
censored material has been cut

explanation.surface: A husband's programme was censored after it went out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'number two' is a very short crop, named for the clipper guard size.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbers grade clipper cuts by number, so a number two is one style of crop.

clue.text: Merriest imp messed about in high office

indicators.note: letters messed about are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gleeful little devil causing chaos in a top government post.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of government holds one of the most senior posts in the state.
